steps: Identify and treat the PRECIPITANT (GI bleed, sepsis/SBP, constipation, hypokalaemia, dehydration, sedatives).
Lactulose titrated to 2–3 soft stools/day (oral or enema).
Add rifaximin for inadequate response / secondary prevention.
Avoid sedatives; do not over-restrict protein; correct electrolytes.
Manage underlying cirrhosis; assess for transplant.

drugRefs.dose: 30–45 mL (20–30 g) titrated to 2–3 soft stools/day; if unable to take orally, give as retention enema (300 mL lactulose in 700 mL water)
drugRefs.freq: 2–4 times daily, titrated to stool output
drugRefs.why: Acidifies the gut lumen and traps/clears ammonia; dose is titrated to 2–3 soft stools per day.
Reduces ammonia-producing gut flora; added for inadequate response to lactulose and for secondary prevention of recurrence.

refs: Harrison's Principles of Internal Medicine, 22e — Cirrhosis and Its Complications
AASLD/EASL Practice Guideline — Hepatic Encephalopathy in Chronic Liver Disease

confirm: Confusion/asterixis with chronic liver disease or porto-systemic shunt; a precipitant (GI bleed, infection, constipation, electrolytes, sedatives) is usually present.
